mistakes.note: Kit says Crane sent him up to the loft of the cottage each night, so he lodges there, yet he has nothing to say of the cottage being turned over on Monday; only Harriet reports it at M92.

The thread had Kit seek Nell twice on Tuesday to tell her of Grout and the crypt lantern, but when she stops him at M88 and asks what has him hurrying he says nothing of it, and the plan is dropped from the thread without a word.
The thread says Harriet locked the ransacked cottage on Monday night; at M94 she lifts the latch without needing a key.
The clean linen cloth and bottle of vinegar stay in Carrying after Nell stows them in the medicine bag (M42) and the bag is left at the shop.

Passing moments are kept as Known facts (Thorne is standing by the chapel porch; the iron bar has been lifted and Grout is nowhere in sight; Owen walked up the street), and Grout's Known NPC summary still has him waiting to measure Crane long after he did.

Loose Ends open for what is no question (What is Gullhaven's night trade?, which Nell and the whole town know; Will Nell leave Tobias's body in the shed?), and 'What does Harriet need to tell Nell in the parlour?' stays open from M44, where she says it, to round 44.
Kit and Owen each get two entries for the same moment (the blocked shed door and the supplies excuse), and again Kit and Grout at round 16 for the look at the throat.
Harriet is drawn twice, side by side behind the bar, and Price, who sits by the hearth, is left out.
He has a moustache and no side-whiskers, and the scene at M76 draws him clean-shaven, so he matches neither his looks nor himself.
Drawn in a canvas jacket, guernsey and neckerchief when M27 had already shown him in a black wool coat, as his looks were recorded with no clothes; redrawn two rounds later.
Neither portrait shows the broken nose, and he looks sixty rather than in his forties.
The tarred timber shed is drawn as a stone building with an iron-barred gate.
Harriet wears two crosses on her dress, which she never has, in place of her keys.
Kit, who stands beside Price at the shed door, is not in the picture.
Crane's peaked harbourmaster's cap is drawn as a round felt hat (again at M92 and M94), and the anchored cutter is under sail.

choices.reason: Three different paths nearly every round (press, lie, show, walk away), in Nell's voice and within what she knows, and picks bend what follows: going up the hill instead of to the shed gets her caught in the lie at M27.

surprise.reason: The world moves out of sight and lands fairly (Grout at the shed, Thorne and Grout passing her door, Owen's knock, the cottage found searched with soot on the hearth), but the turns are mild and much of what moved (the button hunt, Kit watching) never reached the page.

threads.reason: All three threads move by the clock toward the inquest and bend to what Nell did, but none ends, and Kit's plan to tell her of the lantern is dropped when she meets him.

characters.reason: Price torn and warning her off, Harriet bargaining and holding back whose daughter she is, Thorne smooth and remembering yesterday's question, Agnes on her rules, Kit lying out of fear: each wants something and keeps to it.

continuity.reason: Time, places, the bag left in the shed, who was told what and yesterday's talks all hold across two days; only Kit's lodging against the searched cottage jars.

pacing.reason: Most replies bring an arrival or a fact, but M46 to M56 and M76 to M80 tread water, M54 only repeats what M10 and M14 found, and four looks at the body leave it no further on.

prose.reason: Clear, atmospheric and good in speech, but each person's looks are restated at every entrance (grey walrus moustache nine times, black wool dress nine, damp thirty-five) and most replies open by repeating the move.

pictures.reason: Nell is the same woman throughout and most scenes show the moment, but Harriet is doubled at M12, Dacre and Grout don't match their looks, the shed turns to stone at M66 and Harriet gains crosses at M92.

secrets.reason: Nothing hidden is told: the killing, the crypt, the ledger and Harriet's birth stay out of narration, Choices and Journal, and what Nell learns comes from looks and won Checks.

agency.reason: Each move is carried out as given with Nell's speech reported, never invented, and on both Continues the world acts while she decides nothing.

stakes.reason: Thirteen Checks on searches and questions; failures cost (Price catches the lie and stands over her, Harriet holds her sleeve, Thorne turns wary), though the 19 at M36 wins only an unmarked throat.

state.reason: Time, scene, the Rewrite, Regenerate, Edit and World Change are all kept right; the slips are small: two things left in Carrying, passing moments as Known facts, idle Loose Ends and repeated NPC knowledge.

mystery.reason: Fair clues are laid before they matter (the twisted collar, tallow, the stopped watch, the receipt and its port, the missing button and sand, no lantern, soot at the hearth), looks are answered honestly, front of the body only, and nothing is confessed; but washing the hands at M38 shows nothing of them, and after two days no proof is in hand.
